theorem.attribution: Published classical front-door sufficient identification theorem, specialized to a single observed front-door variable in the declared finite binary SCM.

scientific_scope.model: Known static recursive SCM, explicit observed/latent partition, independent structural errors.
scientific_scope.variables: At most eight binary listed nodes, including explicit non-root latent variables.
scientific_scope.target: One observed treatment X and one distinct observed outcome Y, full interventional distribution.
scientific_scope.selector: One observed distinct variable; explicit request checked without substitution, null permits finite singleton search.
scientific_scope.information: Compatible full observed population law with separately reviewed strict observed-joint positivity, stronger than theorem support requirements.
scientific_scope.extra_assumptions: No linearity, Gaussianity, faithfulness, or scientific approval inferred by the software.
scientific_scope.review: Separate typed, input-bound research declarations; not reviewer authentication.
scientific_scope.output: Canonical nested observable functional, distinct intervention and marginal treatment value roles, no numeric estimation.
scientific_scope.failure: Unsupported criterion is not general nonidentification.

mapping.claim: Classical sufficient criterion, observable formula and P(x,m)>0. The project uses conservative observed-joint positivity.
Graph/path criterion and outgoing-edge transformations. Singleton search only; not the paper's set enumeration algorithm.

independence.production: Reachability after removing the candidate, ancestral moralization in two outgoing-edge-deleted graphs.
independence.replay: Simple directed path enumeration and independently enumerated active paths with transitive closure. Independent formula reconstruction.
independence.shared: Existing strict shape/population validation, type and hashing primitives. Production reuses the existing moralization primitive; replay does not.
independence.limitation: Finite arithmetic and graphical tests supplement the sufficient theorem; neither a formal proof nor completeness claim.

business_interface.review_rule: Separate source/role reading review and FrontdoorReview; no automatic scientific approval.
